chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Regarding a man who owes something and then settles (compounds the debt), he said: 'If it is with the good pleasure/contentment of his creditor, then there is no harm.'

key_terms.يُصَالِحُ: to settle or compound a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid debt settlement (sulh) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a debt settlement (sulh) is valid provided the creditor agrees with genuine contentment (bitibati nafsihi), emphasizing the spiritual dimension of financial transactions in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the principle that mutual consent, free from coercion or hidden resentment, is the cornerstone of permissible commercial agreements. This ruling aligns with the broader ethical imperative in Shia tradition to prioritize harmony and goodwill in interpersonal dealings.
